plan.goal: Doxorubicin dose-response on HepG2 spheroids: one spheroid per well in a 96-well ULA plate, 1000 cells/spheroid, dosed from a 5 mM DMSO stock at 5 µM working concentration.
plan.rationale: HepG2 spheroids formed at 1000 cells/spheroid of 20 µm cells give ~200 µm diameter at solid packing (~221 µm at realistic 0.74 packing), which is within the ≤~200-400 µm range that avoids necrotic cores (O2 penetration ~200 µm; necrotic fraction = 0). One spheroid per well in a 96-well ULA plate uses the standard 100 µL working volume. Doxorubicin is delivered from a 5 mM DMSO stock at 5 µM working concentration, giving a 0.1% v/v DMSO vehicle fraction — at the upper edge of the ≤0.1% guideline and well below the ~0.5% cytotoxic threshold. HepG2 is an immortalized hepatoma line (BSL-1), not primary material; doubling 48-60 h.
caveats: DMSO vehicle fraction is 0.1% v/v — at the upper edge of the ≤0.1% guideline; include a matched vehicle-only control (0.1% DMSO) to isolate solvent effects.
Spheroid diameter ~221 µm at realistic packing is near the ~200 µm O2 penetration limit; monitor for core necrosis if spheroids grow larger over the 72 h culture.
HepG2 is an immortalized hepatoma line (BSL-1), not primary hepatocytes — metabolic phenotype differs from primary material.
Confirm spheroid formation (single spheroid per well, no aggregation) by microscopy before dosing.
Doxorubicin is light-sensitive and a cytotoxic agent — handle per institutional safety and light-protection protocols.
